'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
**[[Attacks on civilians in the Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
***[[Russian Armed Forces|Russian forces]] strike a residential area in [[Zaporizhzhia]], injuring 18 [[civilian]]s, including six children. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/russia-keeps-air-strikes-kyiv-nato-meets-2023-07-12/ (Reuters)]
***An 81-year-old man is killed and his wife is injured due to Russian shelling in [[Kherson]]. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2023/jul/13/russia-ukraine-war-at-a-glance-what-we-know-on-day-505-of-the-invasion (''The Guardian'')]
*[[Israeli–Lebanese conflict]]
**Three [[Hezbollah]] members are injured by [[Israel]]i strikes near the [[Blue Line (border)|Blue Line]] with the [[Israel Defense Forces]] accusing Hezbollah of attempting to destroy the [[border barrier]]. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20230712-israeli-fire-wounds-hezbollah-members-near-lebanon-israel-border-security-source (AFP via France 24)]
*[[Insurgency in Balochistan]]
**Nine [[Pakistan Army|soldiers]], five Tehreek-e-Jihad Pakistan gunmen, and a civilian passerby are killed in a [[shootout]] at a [[security checkpoint]] in [[Zhob]], [[Balochistan, Pakistan|Balochistan]], [[Pakistan]]. Five other soldiers are injured. [https://apnews.com/article/pakistan-militants-attack-security-forces-4609bc60ace91501d0567df370f3ab4f (AP)]

'''Arts and culture'''
*[[Censorship in the Philippines]]
**The [[Philippines]]' [[Movie and Television Review and Classification Board|film review board]] requests that [[Cinema of the United States|American]] [[film distributor]] [[Warner Bros. Pictures]] censor a scene in the upcoming film ''[[Barbie (film)|Barbie]]'' that includes a map displaying the [[Territorial disputes in the South China Sea|internationally contested]] [[nine-dash line]] in the [[South China Sea]] before releasing the film in the country. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-66173164 (BBC News)]
*In a study published in ''[[PLOS One]]'', researchers identify subtle modifications to [[Art of ancient Egypt|ancient Egyptian]] [[funerary art]]works, such as the repositioning of [[Ramesses II]]'s [[sceptre]] and changes in the [[pigment]]ation used for [[skin color]], using [[Portable magnetic resonance imaging|portable imaging]] and [[Analytical chemistry|chemical analysis]] techniques. These findings suggest a higher degree of creativity among ancient Egyptian artists than was previously recognized. [https://www.manilatimes.net/2023/07/13/world/americas-emea/ancient-egyptian-artists-altered-their-work-study-shows/1900421 (AFP via ''The Manila Times'')]

'''Business and economy'''
*[[2022–2023 Pakistani economic crisis]]
**The [[International Monetary Fund]] approves a [[United States dollar|US$]]3 billion [[bailout]] deal for [[Economy of Pakistan|Pakistan]] to avert its potential [[National debt of Pakistan|debt]] [[Sovereign default|default]]s and regain [[economic stability]]. [https://apnews.com/article/pakistan-imf-bailout-approved-81bc70d9d707534ae3ffbba9030e8add (AP)]
*[[2022–2023 food crises]]
**[[India]]'s [[Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution|food ministry]] reports a 341% surge in [[tomato]] prices from {{Indian Rupee|24.68|link=yes}} (US$0.30) to {{Indian Rupee|108.92}} ($1.33) per kilogram, attributed to extreme weather and the [[tomato mosaic virus]] affecting major tomato-producing [[States and union territories of India|states]]. [[Agriculture in India|Farmers]] have reported incidents of tomato theft in response to the report. [https://www.cnbc.com/2023/07/13/indias-tomato-prices-surge-over-300percent-prompting-thieves-and-turmoil.html (CNBC)]
*[[Tourism in Indonesia]]
**[[Bali]] announces the imposition of a [[Indonesian rupiah|IDR]]{{nbsp}}150,000 (US$10) [[tourist tax]] for foreign visitors from 2024, aiming to preserve [[Culture of Bali|the island's culture]] and environment. [https://www.arabnews.com/node/2336521/world (AFP via ''Arab News'')]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[Tornadoes of 2023]]
**A series of [[tornado]]es strike [[Chicago]], [[Illinois]], [[United States]], prompting complete [[ground stop]]s at [[O'Hare International Airport|O'Hare]] and [[Midway International Airport]]s. [https://www.fox32chicago.com/news/chicago-flights-canceled-severe-weather-impacting-travel (WFLD-TV)]
*Three people are killed and 14 others are injured when a [[Greyhound Lines|Greyhound]] passenger bus crashes into three parked trucks at a [[Rest area|rest area]] off [[Interstate 70 in Illinois|Interstate 70]] in [[Madison County, Illinois]], U.S. [https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2023/jul/12/greyhound-bus-crash-illinois (AP via ''The Guardian'')]

'''International relations'''
*[[Iran–Russia relations]]
**[[Iran]] summons the [[Russia]]n ambassador over a joint statement issued by Russia and the [[Gulf Cooperation Council]] over three islands disputed by the [[United Arab Emirates]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/iran-summons-russian-ambassador-over-statement-three-islands-state-media-2023-07-12/ (Reuters)]
*[[Japan–North Korea relations]], [[North Korea–United States relations]]
**[[North Korea]] fires a [[Hwasong-18]] [[intercontinental ballistic missile]] into waters near [[Japan]]. This comes a day after North Korea threatened the [[United States]], claiming that an American [[Surveillance aircraft|spy plane]] entered the country's [[exclusive economic zone]] multiple times on Monday. [https://apnews.com/article/north-korea-missile-launch-ced1ccd42f6e9d3aafdd02f3e77572fb (AP)] [https://edition.cnn.com/2023/07/11/asia/north-korea-missile-test-intl-hnk-ml/index.html (CNN)]
*[[Myanmar–Thailand relations]], [[Myanmar civil war (2021–present)|Myanmar civil war]]
**[[Deputy Prime Minister of Thailand|Thai deputy prime minister]] and [[Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Thailand)|foreign minister]] [[Don Pramudwinai]] announces that he visited jailed [[Myanmar]] [[National League for Democracy|democracy]] leader [[Aung San Suu Kyi]] last week, becoming the first known foreign representative to meet with the [[deposed]] [[State Counsellor of Myanmar|state counsellor]] since the [[2021 Myanmar coup d'état|2021 coup d'état]]. [https://www.channelnewsasia.com/asia/aung-san-suu-kyi-thai-fm-says-he-met-ousted-myanmar-leader-3623241 (AFP via CNA)]
*[[2023 Vilnius summit]]
**At the [[NATO summit]] in [[Vilnius]], [[Lithuania]], [[G7]] officials announce that they have unveiled an international framework for [[Ukraine]]’s long-term security in a effort to boost their defense against [[Russia]] and deter them from any future aggression. The measures will include bilateral talks, military hardware, training, intelligence-sharing, and other plans to rebuild the [[Economy of Ukraine|country’s economy]]. [https://www.politico.eu/article/embargo-g7-countries-pledge-long-term-support-to-ukraine/amp/ (Politico EU)] [https://www.reuters.com/world/sending-message-russia-g7-announce-long-term-security-assurances-ukraine-2023-07-12/ (Reuters)]
*[[Serbia–United States relations]]
**The United States imposes sanctions on [[Aleksandar Vulin]], a top Serbian official considered "Moscow's man". [https://news.yahoo.com/us-imposes-sanctions-top-serbian-172612717.html (Yahoo! News)]
*[[UNESCO]] accepts the U.S. as a member after it withdrew from the organization in 2018. [https://www.euronews.com/2023/06/30/unesco-accepts-the-us-back-into-the-fold-after-a-five-year-absence (Euronews)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Prime Minister of Singapore|Singaporean prime minister]] [[Lee Hsien Loong]] places [[Ministry of Transport (Singapore)|Transport Minister]] [[S. Iswaran]] on an immediate leave of absence amid an ongoing corruption investigation by the [[Corrupt Practices Investigation Bureau]] into Iswaran and other individuals. [https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/singapore-anti-graft-agency-probes-transport-minister-2023-07-12/ (Reuters)]
*Six people are killed during protests in [[Nairobi]], [[Kenya]], against [[Kenyan taxation system|tax]] increases imposed by [[President of Kenya|President]] [[William Ruto]]'s [[Government of Kenya|government]], in which the [[Kenya Police|police]] have employed [[tear gas]] and heightened security measures. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20230712-kenya-police-fire-tear-gas-as-protesters-defy-ban (AFP via France 24)]
 
'''Politics and elections'''
*Aftermath of the [[2023 Guatemalan general election]]
**At the request of the [[Guatemala]]n Public Ministry, a judge orders the [[Supreme Electoral Tribunal (Guatemala)|Supreme Electoral Tribunal]] to suspend the legal personality of candidate [[Bernardo Arévalo]]'s [[Semilla (political party)|Movimiento Semilla]] party, which went on to the second round of elections on 20 August. The legal measure would leave Arévalo out of the election. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2023/jul/13/guatemala-prosecutor-suspends-party-of-anti-corruption-election-candidate (''The Guardian'')]
**After several days of delay, the [[Supreme Electoral Tribunal (Guatemala)|Supreme Electoral Tribunal]] makes the electoral results official and calls for the second round of elections between [[Sandra Torres]] and Bernardo Arévalo. [https://abcnews.go.com/International/wireStory/guatemalan-tribunal-certifies-election-results-minutes-after-court-101201509 (AP via ABC News)]
*Aftermath of the [[2023 Thai general election]]
**[[Thailand]]'s [[Election Commission of Thailand|election commission]] petitions the [[Constitutional Court of Thailand|Constitutional Court]] to suspend leading [[Prime Minister of Thailand|prime ministerial]] candidate [[Pita Limjaroenrat]], alleging his violation of campaign laws due to prior [[Share (finance)|share]] ownership in a [[media company]], [[iTV (Thailand)|iTV]]. [https://www.lemonde.fr/en/international/article/2023/07/12/thai-electoral-body-recommends-suspension-of-top-candidate-for-prime-minister_6050423_4.html (AFP via ''Le Monde'')]
*[[LGBT rights in Indonesia]]
**An [[ASEAN]] [[LGBT event]] scheduled in [[Indonesia]] is relocated to an undisclosed location due to received security threats and [[anti-LGBT rhetoric]] from various groups. [https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/lgbt-event-indonesia-scrapped-after-security-threats-2023-07-12/ (Reuters)]
